1) typed Prolog and λ-Prolog have a strict type discipline based on simple types; 2) this type discipline does not handle well common logic programming practices; 3) the head-condition is at heart of the problem; 4) a second-order scheme is proposed to enforce the head-condition and solve the problem; 5) this scheme has been implemented in the Teyjus Prolog system and is available in a prototype version.
1) the head condition can be enforced by parametric polymorphism; 2) the parametric polymorphism is compatible with the concrete notation of typed Prolog and λ-Prolog programs.
